sources.entry: Mos - Smooth your mouse's scrolling and reverse the mouse scroll direction

summary.one_liner: Mos is a free, open-source macOS menu bar utility that smooths mouse wheel scrolling, lets you reverse scroll direction per axis, and remaps mouse buttons.
summary.what_it_does: Mos intercepts mouse wheel events on macOS and converts them into interpolated, smoother scrolling, with adjustable minimum step, speed gain and duration, and an optional simulated trackpad mode. Vertical and horizontal axes can be smoothed and reversed independently. Settings can be global or overridden per application, and each app can inherit or customize scroll, hotkey and button rules. Mouse, keyboard or custom events can be recorded and bound to system actions, shortcuts, opening apps, files or scripts, with a built-in action library covering Mission Control, Spaces switching, screenshots and Finder operations. The README also describes Logitech button support through Bolt, Unifying and Bluetooth-direct devices via Logi/HID++. Installation is by manual download of Mos.app from GitHub Releases or via Homebrew cask, and it requires granting macOS accessibility permission.
use_cases: smooth out choppy mouse wheel scrolling on a mac
reverse scroll direction for a mouse but not the trackpad
remap extra mouse buttons to shortcuts or system actions
bind a mouse button to open an app or run a script
configure different scroll behavior for each application
use Logitech mouse buttons on macOS
how_to_run: Or download the latest Mos.app from GitHub Releases and move it to /Applications
Launch Mos and grant it accessibility permission in macOS settings
notable: Per-axis control: vertical and horizontal scrolling can be smoothed and reversed separately
Per-application overrides that can inherit global settings or customize scrolling and button bindings
Button bindings can target system actions, keyboard shortcuts, apps, scripts or files
Logi/HID++ support for Logitech Bolt, Unifying and Bluetooth-direct devices
caveats: Requires macOS 10.13 or later, and needs macOS accessibility permission to read and rewrite scroll events
License is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) and the README asks that it not be uploaded to the App Store
README notes that changes touching Logi/HID, accessibility, signing or update logic are higher risk and should be discussed first; it is not a general-purpose contribution-open project
